content: Cefixime, commonly sold under the brand name Suprax, is a cephalosporin antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It is effective only against bacterial infections and does not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. How to Use: Cefixime is taken orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor. It is typically taken once daily, but in children, it may be prescribed twice daily (every 12 hours). The dosage depends on the patient’s medical condition and response to treatment. For optimal results, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. It is important to complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days, to prevent the infection from returning. Side Effects: Common side effects include stomach upset, abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, gas, headache, or dizziness. While these effects are usually mild, contact your doctor if they persist or worsen. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition called Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea, which can occur during or even weeks to months after treatment. Prolonged or repeated use of cefixime may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions are rare but may include rash, itching, swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience these symptoms. Precautions: Before taking cefixime, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, other cephalosporins (e.g., cephalexin), or penicillins, as cross-reactivity may occur. Additionally, disclose any other allergies or medical conditions. This medication may interfere with live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine) and certain lab tests, potentially causing false results. The chewable form of cefixime may contain aspartame, which should be avoided by individuals with phenylketonuria (PKU). During pregnancy, cefixime should only be used when clearly needed, and it is unknown if it passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how cefixime works or increase the risk of side effects. Provide your doctor and pharmacist with a complete list of all medications, supplements, and herbal products you are using. This medication may interfere with certain diabetic urine tests, leading to false results. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store cefixime at room temperature (20-25°C or 68-77°F) away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard any unused or expired medication as instructed by your pharmacist or local waste disposal company. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless directed to do so. Overdose: In case of overdose, seek immediate medical attention. If the individual has severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center (1-800-222-1222 in the U.S. or 1-844-764-7669 in Canada). Important Notes: This summary does not contain all possible information about cefixime. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
